title: Number of Flowers in Full Bloom
summary: Given a 0-indexed 2D integer array flowers indicating the start and end times of each flower's full bloom, and a 0-indexed integer array people indicating the arrival times of each person, return an integer array answer where answer[i] represents the number of flowers in full bloom when the i^th person arrives.
statement: Given a 0-indexed 2D integer array flowers indicating the start and end times of each flower's full bloom, and a 0-indexed integer array people indicating the arrival times of each person, return an integer array answer where answer[i] represents the number of flowers in full bloom when the i^th person arrives.
constraints: Each bloom interval [start,end] is inclusive at both endpoints.
For each arrival time, count intervals satisfying start<=time<=end.
Return counts in the same order as the people input, including repeated arrival times.
reference_solution:
def flowers_in_bloom(flowers,people):
    from bisect import bisect_left,bisect_right
    starts=sorted(start for start,_ in flowers);ends=sorted(end for _,end in flowers)
    return [bisect_right(starts,time)-bisect_left(ends,time) for time in people]

def flowers_in_bloom(flowers,people):
    from bisect import bisect_left,bisect_right
    starts=sorted(start for start,_ in flowers);ends=sorted(end for _,end in flowers)
    return [bisect_left(starts,time)-bisect_left(ends,time) for time in people]
hints: At time t, blooming flowers equal those that have started minus those that ended before t.
Sort all starts and ends independently and use binary-search insertion positions.
The first count includes starts at t, while the subtracted count excludes ends at t, exactly matching inclusive intervals.
